source.title: Invariant Learning Dynamics of Transformers in Inductive Reasoning Tasks
source.authors: Tiberiu Musat; Tiago Pimentel; Nicolas Zucchet; Thomas Hofmann

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether the same task and architecture converge to one identifiable algorithm across runs, using an initialization sweep and circuit identification rather than the grokking setup.
record.gate_note: The paper cites grokking as motivation but does not measure delayed test generalization after overfitting. Its initialization experiments directly test V6 by identifying which induction circuit wins across runs.
record.test_reason: No grokking (no delayed generalization), but V6 is stated generally. The 3-layer initialization scan shows which identifiable circuit a network trained on one task converges to. This is a new setting (in-context bigrams, IMIR-constrained SGD) with a result on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct, but incomplete. The authors also frame all three winners as induction-head circuits in different layer pairs. They call the setup simplified and note that the winner is hard to predict from a circuit's own initial strengths.
record.recipe_differences: Studies synthetic in-context bigram and multi-hop induction tasks with attention-only transformers and circuit-coordinate analysis; it does not reproduce the grokking training recipe or measure delayed test generalization.
record.method_sensitivity: The winning induction circuit changes with the initial strengths of β and β′′.
record.problems: The initialization-dependent winners are evaluated in a simplified synthetic setup. The phase-transition plot reports no exact counts or uncertainty, and circuit identification uses a fixed evaluation batch.

untested.parts: No train/test accuracy delay, no algorithmic dataset, no training-set-size sweep.
Circuit units are tracked continuously, but there is no grokking jump, no removal of memorizing components, and no test of whether progress measures predict a jump.
No initialization-scale or weight-norm switch of grokking delays; no non-algorithmic data.
No weight decay, no efficiency account, no critical dataset size, no ungrokking.
Not tested on grokking tasks such as modular arithmetic. Variation across architectures and hyperparameters is not tested. Unconstrained training is not tested.

missing.what: Two trained 5-layer two-hop models recover different circuits. C1 uses layers 1, 3, 4 plus three aiding units; C2 uses layers 1, 2, 3 plus one aiding unit. Essentials-only accuracy is 0.594 vs 0.719.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is about induction-circuit dynamics and cites grokking only as motivation. The V6 link is indirect: the variation is in where one algorithm is implemented, not which algorithm is learned. Initialization was engineered (other directions zeroed) and dynamics were projected onto the IMIR, which limits how far the results generalize to ordinary training.

versions.untested_parts: No small algorithmic-dataset train/test-accuracy trajectories, overfitting-to-generalization delay, or training-set-size sweep.
The paper studies induction-circuit learning dynamics, but not a grokking generalization jump, removal of memorizing components after overfitting, or continuous measures predicting such a jump.
No non-algorithmic data or initialization-scale/weight-norm sweep testing grokking-like delays.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning.
No weight-decay/low-norm efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking test.
Tests initialization-dependent circuit choice in a simplified three-layer in-context-bigram setup; does not test variation across architectures or hyperparameters.
No adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax artifact controls.

rows.subject: 3-layer, 1-head-per-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Train on in-context bigrams while varying the initial strengths of β and β′′; identify the winning circuit by post-training causal ablation.

conditions.value: (sβ, sβ′′) sampled from Uniform(0, 0.6)²; other IMIR directions zeroed

rows.value: Three distinct circuits win in different initialization regions: (α, β, γ), (α, β′, γ′), and (α′, β′′, γ′).
rows.locator: Section 4.3 and Figure 4; training details in Appendix E.1
rows.note: The text describes three distinct solutions and initialization-dependent winners; the phase-transition plot gives no exact region counts.
rows.check: Not a clear reversal. All three winners are the same induction-head algorithm (previous-token, match, readout) placed in different layer pairs. Convergence holds at the algorithm level but varies at the implementation level. Training was projected onto a 7-dim sub-manifold, with only β and β′′ initialized nonzero, so this is not ordinary random initialization. Region sizes are given only in the figure.

source_check.correct: State: observed for V6. The three solutions implement induction using layer pairs (1,2), (1,3), and (2,3); initialization changes circuit placement without demonstrating different algorithms.
source_check.problem: The partial state treats different implementations of the same induction algorithm as incomplete algorithmic convergence.

rows.subject: 3-layer, 1-head-per-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Train random seeds on the same in-context-bigram task and track the seven named circuit units.
rows.measure: Circuit units growing together, indicating the winning circuit
rows.value: The training-dynamics plot shows different winning circuits across seeds.
rows.note: The text says the units that grow together indicate which of the three competing circuits wins; per-seed outcomes are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: Same caveat as R1: the seeds differ in which layer pair hosts the induction circuit, not in the algorithm. Training was IMIR-constrained. Per-seed outcomes are figure-only.

source_check.correct: State: observed for V6. The 12-seed dynamics track competing implementations of the same induction algorithm, distinguished by their circuit units and layer pairs.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.3; Appendix E.1; Appendix E.2, Figure 7 caption.
source_check.problem: Different winning circuit placements do not establish partial convergence to the same algorithm.

relationships.condition: 3-layer, single-head attention-only transformers on all-rare in-context bigrams, with IMIR-constrained SGD and β/β′′ initial strengths varied
relationships.reason: All runs converge to an induction-head algorithm, but which layer-pair circuit wins depends on initialization, with sharp phase boundaries (R1, R2). So convergence holds at the algorithm level, not the circuit level.
relationships.display_finding: All runs converged to an induction-head algorithm, but initialization selected the winning layer-pair circuit with sharp phase boundaries.

tranche.reason: The constrained in-context-bigram setting supplies results on V6 beyond the original grokking setting.

source_check.notes: These results concern constrained induction training, without a delayed-generalization measurement. Section 4.3 allows circuit compositions; boundaries are sharp between blue and the other solutions, but not between green and red.

statements.correction: Three-layer single-head transformers; IMIR-constrained SGD; initialization-dependent induction-circuit layer pairs; same induction algorithm across these implementations; supports V6 in this tested setting.
statements.problem: The description of initialization-dependent layer placement is accurate, but its limits_scope classification does not follow for V6, which concerns algorithm identity.
